issue.title: internal/agent: TestDesktopHandlerNeedsItsEntryAndProgram red on Windows: no exe found for an entry there
issue.body:
Seen on the Windows box (win-run, xiaomi-gpu, Windows 11, go1.26.8) at origin/main f4c664a09, run alone (`go test -count=1 -run ... ./internal/agent`), and the same in a full internal/agent run there. Not in #1827, #4115 or #4786. Windows CI only compiles the tests, so nothing else shows it. Found while porting coffemon's patches; not taking it.

```
--- FAIL: TestDesktopHandlerNeedsItsEntryAndProgram (0.05s)
    desktop_handler_test.go:35: an entry there: exe "" found false err <nil>, want "C:\\Users\\yeton\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\TestDesktopHandlerNeedsItsEntryAndProgram1837619228\\003\\Cindy.AppImage"
```

The fixture is a Linux .desktop handler with an AppImage; on Windows the lookup finds nothing. Either the test needs to force the Linux path or skip on Windows.

comments.body:
A test-only fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5069-desktop-test-windows-skip), commit [1da2a7ebd](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/1da2a7ebd0874a935386aa59aa13de6462116a5f), based on `ed0ab567`.

`TestDesktopHandlerNeedsItsEntryAndProgram` builds a Linux XDG `.desktop` fixture, but Windows resolves link handlers from the registry instead, so the fixture never covered Windows and the test fails there for that reason alone. It now skips on Windows with that explanation; the Linux assertions and fixtures are unchanged.

The related Linux race run passes and the package compiles for `GOOS=windows`; the Windows binary was compiled only, not executed. No production change. AI-assisted implementation and review.

issue.title: agent: TestCodexOwnModelsFollowPicks red on Windows (74 allocations, want at most 20)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Red on Windows at untouched origin/main 191f3c0af (xiaomi-gpu, Windows 11, Go 1.26.8, `win-run go test -count=1 ./internal/agent/`):

```
--- FAIL: TestCodexOwnModelsFollowPicks (0.18s)
    codex_own_test.go:53: a look at Codex's ticks made 74 allocations, want at most 20
```

Searched by name: not in #4786, #4115, #1827, #1388, #2808. It is an allocation bar like #4786's six, and 74 is in the range those read there (67 to 82), so likely the same cause: `provider.StampNow`'s `environSum` makes a string per environment variable on Windows each call. Not traced further; the other 24 agent reds in the same run are already filed (#4115, #4786, #4785, #5068, #5069, #5070, #5130, #5343, #5344, #1827, #1388, #2808, #4033, #2775, #5019).

issue.title: Windows: PowerShell agy function starts agy without the gateway key (GUI magpie.exe not waited for)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

On Windows, with agy on a magpie model, typing `agy` in PowerShell starts the real agy without the gateway or its key:

```
modelProvider is set to "gemini" in settings.json, but the GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable is not set. ...
```

The profile block (`# >>> magpie agy >>>`) is there and `magpie agy env` prints all three lines from Git Bash.

## Cause

`agyFunction`'s PowerShell body (`internal/agent/agy.go`) reads the variables with

```powershell
foreach ($l in @(& 'C:\...\magpie.exe' agy env)) { ... }
```

`magpie.exe` is a GUI-subsystem program (PE subsystem 2; `magpie.com` is 3). PowerShell doesn't wait for a GUI program it runs outside a pipeline, so `@(& magpie.exe agy env)` is empty, `$start.model` is unset, and the function falls through to `& $real @args` with no `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`. The comment above the function already says PowerShell doesn't wait for the GUI app; the call that reads `agy env` has the same problem.

Measured on Windows 11, magpie at v0.1.x (`.local\bin\magpie.exe`, Nov 6 build):

| Call | PowerShell 7.6 | Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@(& magpie.exe agy env).Count` | 0 | 0 |
| `@(& magpie.exe agy env \| ForEach-Object { $_ }).Count` | 3 | 3 |
| `@(& magpie.com agy env).Count` | 3 | — |

## Fix

Read `agy env` through a pipeline (`& prog agy env | ForEach-Object { ... }`), which PowerShell waits on for GUI and console programs alike, so it holds whether or not a `magpie.com` is beside the app.

Workaround until it ships: in the profile block, replace `magpie.exe` with `magpie.com`, then `. $PROFILE`.
